task.title: Look at the sources of a fact
task.shortdesc: See which books and records are listed for a birth, a death or another fact, and add one.

prereq.p: Open the page of Emily Brontë first. shows how.

context.p: Each fact on a person's page has a small chip that counts its sources. This page adds a source to the death of Emily Brontë.
The sheet that the chip opens lists the sources that are already in the tree. The sample tree has some. If your tree has none, the list is empty until you add a source, as shows.

info.p: It starts with and a number, and ends with +. An event has one too.

stepresult.p: A sheet named opens. It lists the sources of that fact. A fact with none says No sources for this fact yet.

step.cmd: Choose at the foot of the sheet.

stepresult.p: A list named opens. It has a box named , a button named , and the sources already in your tree.

step.cmd: Choose the source that backs the fact.

info.p: If it is not in the list, choose and fill in the form. shows how to add a source to a person.

stepresult.p: A second step opens, with the title of the source at the top.

step.cmd: In , type where to look in the source.

info.p: For the Haworth burial register, type Burials of December 1848.

step.cmd: In , choose how much weight the source deserves.

info.p: The box starts at . The step also has and boxes for the words of the entry. You can leave them empty. For a copy that someone typed out, is a fair choice, as the picture shows.

stepresult.p: The sheet shows the source again, now on the list.
The chip on the page shows one more source.

result.p: Each source on the sheet shows its title. Under it is the page or reference you gave. A source that has an author, or a quality, can show those too, such as Quality: 2 · Secondary evidence. What a line shows depends on what you have entered for that source.
Each source on the sheet has four buttons, named , , and . The sheet also has a button named .
result.note: Good practice: give each fact its own source and its own page. Ask two questions about a source. Is it the original or a copy? Was the writer there at the time?
